served.stem: Which base is strong enough to deprotonate a terminal alkyne (pKa about 25) essentially completely?
choices: Sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3 (the pKa of carbonic acid is about 6)
Sodium acetate (the pKa of acetic acid is about 5)
Sodium hydroxide, NaOH (the pKa of water is about 16)
Sodium amide, NaNH2 (the pKa of ammonia is about 38)
Sodium ethoxide, NaOEt (the pKa of ethanol is about 16)
served.bankWhy: Equilibrium favors the side with the WEAKER acid, the one with the higher pKa. Cross out the metal to find the real base. Amide ion gives ammonia at pKa 38, which is weaker than the alkyne at 25, so the reaction goes forward. Hydroxide would give water at 16, which is stronger than the alkyne, so it does not.

answer.text: Sodium amide, NaNH2 (the pKa of ammonia is about 38)
answer.line: Amide's partner, ammonia, is a far weaker acid than the alkyne, so the proton moves over and stays.

steps: Cross out the sodium. The real base is the anion, and its partner acid is the number in parentheses.
Compare each partner with the alkyne at 25. A proton moves toward the weaker acid, the one with the higher pKa.
Ammonia at 38 sits 13 units above the alkyne, so amide takes the proton essentially completely. Water and ethanol at 16 sit below it, so they hand it back.

choices.text: Sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3 (the pKa of carbonic acid is about 6)
choices.note: Carbonic acid at 6 is a far stronger acid than the alkyne. Bicarbonate is a weak base; the alkyne proton never leaves for it.

choices.text: Sodium acetate (the pKa of acetic acid is about 5)
choices.note: Acetic acid at 5 is stronger still. Its anion is one of the weakest bases here, about 20 units short.

choices.text: Sodium hydroxide, NaOH (the pKa of water is about 16)
choices.note: Hydroxide feels strong, but water at 16 is a stronger acid than the alkyne at 25. The equilibrium sits on the alkyne side.

choices.text: Sodium amide, NaNH2 (the pKa of ammonia is about 38)
choices.note: Ammonia at 38 is the weakest acid in the set, so its anion pulls the alkyne proton for good.

choices.text: Sodium ethoxide, NaOEt (the pKa of ethanol is about 16)
choices.note: Ethoxide makes enolates and runs E2, so it feels strong. Ethanol at 16 is still the stronger acid, so the alkyne stays mostly protonated.

student.lockIt: A base takes a proton for good only when its own partner acid has the higher pKa.
